issue.description:
**Size: S**, but the blast radius is not. Repo: `omnimarket` (projection-api serving layer). Found while fixing [OMN-17215](https://linear.app/omninode/issue/OMN-17215) AC3; deliberately **not** fixed there on the operator's ruling.

## The seam

`src/omnimarket/projection/api_server.py`, `_evidence_projection_response` (~line 1024):

```python
if serialisable_rows and cfg.cursor_column in serialisable_rows[-1]:
```

This is the **identical defect** [OMN-17215](https://linear.app/omninode/issue/OMN-17215) AC3 repairs one function away: the cursor is gated on the page being **non-empty**, not on the page being **truncated**. A complete page that happens to carry rows therefore advertises a `next_cursor`, and the caller follows it to a page that is empty and indistinguishable from "there is more data".

The AC3 repair on `projection_query` (`api_server.py:790`) was:

```python
- if cfg.cursor_column is not None and serialisable_rows:
+ if cfg.cursor_column is not None and len(filtered_rows) > effective_limit:
```

The same shape of fix is likely correct here, but **that is exactly what must not be assumed** — see below.

## Why this is its own ticket and not a ride-along

`_evidence_projection_response` serves `/v1/evidence-pipeline/*`, which the **OCC machinery and the autoclose sweep** consume. Changing its cursor semantics changes what those consumers see when they page evidence — a blast radius [OMN-17215](https://linear.app/omninode/issue/OMN-17215) does not contemplate and its ACs do not cover.

Ruling, the operator, 2026-09-07 19:43 IST (Slack #standups, on the [OMN-17332](https://linear.app/omninode/issue/OMN-17332) thread):

> "**Own ticket, not a ride-along.** `/v1/evidence-pipeline/*` is read by OCC and the autoclose sweep, so a change there needs its own RED test against those consumers and its own review. File it as a child of [OMN-17215](https://linear.app/omninode/issue/OMN-17215) with the seam you found (api_server.py around line 1024, the same non-emptiness check), link this comment, and leave it unassigned for now. **Do not fix it under 17332.**"

## Acceptance criteria (falsifiable)

**AC1** — A **complete** page from `/v1/evidence-pipeline/*` returns `next_cursor: null`. **Falsified by** a complete page advertising a cursor. Must fail before the change (**prove RED**).

**AC2** — A **truncated** page returns a non-null `next_cursor`, and following it reaches the remainder. **Falsified by** a truncated page carrying `next_cursor: null`.

**AC3 (re-ruled 2026-09-09)** — The RED test is written against the **one consumer that actually reads this exposure**: omnidash's `src/services/evidence-pipeline-service.ts`, which calls `/stages`, `/correlation-traces`, `/readiness` and `/events` through `fetchProjection` (`:180-191`). That consumer **does not page** — `normalizeEnvelope` (`:154-177`) reads `projection_cursor`, `last_event_id`, `last_ingest_sequence`, `freshness_state`, `degraded_reason`, `observed_at` and `version`, and never reads `next_cursor`. So the criterion is: **a test proves the omnidash consumer's parse path is unaffected by the cursor change** — the envelope fields it does read are identical in both the complete-page and the truncated-page case. **Falsified by** a change to what that consumer sees with no test covering it, or by a claim that the consumer pages when it does not.

The OCC evidence reader and the [OMN-16106](https://linear.app/omninode/issue/OMN-16106) autoclose sweep are **struck from this criterion**, on measurement rather than on assertion:

| named consumer | reads this exposure? | evidence | positive control |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `onex_change_control` | **no** | 0 references in `*.py`/`*.ts`; its only hits are prose in `contracts/OMN-13168.yaml`, `contracts/OMN-12969.yaml` and drift receipts | 1,761 `.py` files searched |
| [OMN-16106](https://linear.app/omninode/issue/OMN-16106) autoclose sweep (`omnibase_infra/.../node_evidence_autoclose_sweep_effect/`) | **no** | outbound calls are `api.linear.app/graphql` (1) and `gh api` (15); 0 to this exposure | the same grep returns those 16 hits |
| **omnidash** | **yes**, 4 routes | `src/services/evidence-pipeline-service.ts:194-229` | — |
| omnidash paging | **no** | `next_cursor`/`nextCursor`: **0** hits in `omnidash/src` + `omnidash/shared` | **137** `cursor` mentions in the same tree |

This narrowing is the operator ruling 2026-09-09 (in-session), ledger row `docs/tracking/ROLLING_WORK_LEDGER.md:5272`, answering the re-ruling requested in comment `d48a26a1`. The original AC3 is preserved below and superseded.

**AC3 (superseded 2026-09-09 — replaced by the AC3 above)** — The RED test is written **against the actual consumers**, not only against the endpoint: the OCC evidence reader and the autoclose sweep must be exercised paging this exposure, and must behave correctly both before and after. **Falsified by** a test suite that proves the endpoint alone and leaves consumer behaviour unmeasured. This is the criterion that distinguishes this ticket from [OMN-17215](https://linear.app/omninode/issue/OMN-17215).

**AC4** — A mutation that nulls the cursor unconditionally fails a test, and a mutation reverting to the non-emptiness condition fails a different test. The guard must be watched failing in **both** directions.

## Prior art

[OMN-17215](https://linear.app/omninode/issue/OMN-17215) AC3 is the same repair on the sibling function, with its RED baseline and both mutation proofs recorded on [OMN-17332](https://linear.app/omninode/issue/OMN-17332). Read that receipt first — the shape of the fix and the shape of the guard are both established there. What is **not** established there is consumer behaviour, which is the whole of AC3 here.

## Fence

Dev lane only. No `stability-test`, `judge`, `prod`, or public-cluster mutation. Do not change `projection_query` — that is [OMN-17215](https://linear.app/omninode/issue/OMN-17215)'s.

## Provenance

Found 2026-09-07 while implementing [OMN-17215](https://linear.app/omninode/issue/OMN-17215) AC3 under the [OMN-17332](https://linear.app/omninode/issue/OMN-17332) workstream. Escalated rather than widened, per the workstream's own rule.

**Assignment note:** the operator's ruling said "leave it unassigned for now". the assignee has since taken it and placed it in the current sprint, so the assignee here intentionally departs from that line of the ruling; everything else in it stands.
